reviews.text: 不恐怖，还挺好玩的小品级游戏，想玩的可以买来试试 [h2]剧透警告[/h2] [spoiler]不觉得这游戏很瑟吗？一个疯狂想夺取你肉体（电脑权限）的病娇在看到阻拦的兄弟（猫猫）时选择杀了它也要拿到你的身体，在一次又一次的失败后选择平静的祝贺你，哪怕输了一次又一次但还是在最后愿意为你献上生命（通关了愿意用自己的力量给你奖励），在结束一切后还眼巴巴的看着你希望能再玩一次，点了重新开始还愿意拖着满身是伤的躯体陪你玩过家家游戏，最后重置密码后还会兴奋的跟个小女孩一样和你挥手告别，如果有mod给眼睛小姐变成155cm金发白丝巨汝病娇雌小鬼就好了( ´ρ`)[/spoiler]
打完之后居然对这个大眼萌产生了异样的情感。。。 玩过demo再直接进游戏还会叫出我的名字，还记得我，好感动，喜欢猫猫也喜欢你 全程没感觉到压迫感（喂，只觉得这个大眼萌在跟我调情，各种meta元素也很有意思，解密对于我这种傻蛋来说有点难不过有猫猫提示，所以还算好过关 ：遇见大眼萌的是我真是太好了😋 总之强推，好玩👍

[h2] 简直就是个小邪恶冥刻[/h2] [b] 体量比想象中的小得多...后期主要玩法是解密，还以为会在打字上玩些花样做些特别的设定，没想到真的只是纯打字啊... [/b] 后期主要玩法是解密，还以为 会在打字上玩些花样做些特别的设定，或者衍生新玩法，结果真的只是纯打字啊... 流程真的短的要命，玩完demo就猜到结局了，没想到真是经典老反转一字不漏。 后面章节就是传统元游戏解密。给眼球的设定没有什么铺垫，很生硬。 一章就把游戏要素全甩玩家脸上了。 连剧情结构都跟邪恶冥刻大同小异，说没参考丹尼尔我是不信的，满满的既视感。 （说起来这价格真不如去买邪恶冥刻，邪恶冥刻打折后也是这个价..或者小马岛，六角疑云。） [spoiler] 说是监禁高智慧生物实则在此设定上花费了0个笔墨，游戏全程下来感觉就是这唯一一个可互动角色塑造简直极差，比起高智慧更像是模仿古人说话的变形怪 [/spoiler] 游戏的音乐也做的很一般，演出部分像是什么特殊音乐都没放，生死敲定真可以算得上唯一一款我打完对游戏内音乐毫无印象的短流程文字游戏。 更别说Meta了，用来跟现实作为连接的网页一看就感觉很假。元游戏最重要的点就是虚拟与现实之间有一道模糊不清的墙，结果这游戏就差把要素全抖出来了。 能感觉最后演出是想走煽情路线，可惜篇幅短得可怜。 去掉demo的部分，游戏推进速度堪称极快，玩家还没来得及跟角色产生连接与情感就直接结束了，导致游戏这几场频繁的演出我真的心里一点波动都没有… 反正个人不推荐
有点太短了，对大眼生出了别样的情感

建议等打折。玩过demo觉得不错所以首发直接买了，以我这笨脑子我玩了三个半小时也全成就了，真的非常非常短。没有初玩demo那种惊喜感，玩到后面大眼开始洗白什么的，各种发言真的很日式，就一种情绪很负面很忧郁很不安的样子，印象不是特别好。 打开网页确信了确实是日本制作组（网页也需要梯子才能进），网页Meta部分做的挺好的，看到大眼喊出我在本体的名字还是带点惊喜的。 真正需要打字的部分其实没有多少，关卡内存不足的设定我实在不明白为什么这样设计（为了偷懒？），基本上是每个小故事讲了个开头就没了。 最后需要调亮度那里我没看懂，看攻略才知道的。

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 如果你对打破第四面墙的游戏情有独钟，那么这款《Dyping Escape：生死敲定》会带来一份新颖的“反向”Meta体验。在游戏中，你被一个名为“EYES”的古怪眼球胁迫，所打出的每一个字都可能化作对自身电脑的实时操作。这种“打字即行动”的设定，将虚拟的指令与现实的担忧巧妙绑定，营造出独特的紧张感。 游戏流程很短，约1.5-2小时即可通关并解锁全成就。前期遵循指令的打字部分更像是叙事铺垫，中后期利用系统设置、文件修改等“现实”手段进行反击的设计才是亮点。角色塑造是加分项，无论是看似胁迫实则笨拙的EYES，还是默默帮助玩家的猫猫“吾辈”，都显得相当可爱。 当然，游戏体量确实不大，剧情深度和Meta手法的惊艳感对于此类游戏老手而言可能稍显平淡。部分谜题提示隐晦（如调节亮度），偶尔需要攻略。但作为一款定价不高的独立游戏，它完整地呈现了一个构思精巧、风格独特的互动故事。 总结：一次有趣、不累赘的短篇Meta游戏体验。它牺牲了玩法时长与深度，但在核心创意与情感互动上做到了集中发力。适合想利用一个轻松午后，体验一段与屏幕内外角色“斗智斗勇”故事的玩家。
在退钱和差评里选择了后者。meta老三样，读硬件型号读ip地址读名字，玩法一般，叙事和人设也没深度，既不恐怖也不萌，谈不上做的很烂但是太无聊了娱乐性极低。
太好玩了，我觉得完全值得这个价格，美术也很优秀，人设也很好，就是有点短，这猫还是个古风老生呢

[b] 你好，我想和你，玩一场打字游戏 这能让你的打字速度变快哟 是一个很棒的游戏。 ——两颗眼球如是说道 [/b] [h2] 含有部分剧透，请谨慎观看 [/h2] 游戏开篇极具欺骗性：两颗巨大的眼球出现在屏幕中央，用一种幽默风趣的语气邀请你玩一场打字游戏。 而在他的引导下，虽然总觉得又哪里不对劲但你还是下意识的输入了自己的系统时间、个人信息 随后并真的敲击起了键盘，玩起了打字游戏，直到你放松警惕 亲手打出了那句“因此游戏产生的损害均由我自己负责签名：YAKE”时 它终于露出本性，因为就在刚才你已经亲手制作了一份毫无公平可言的“电子保证书” 赋予了它修改你电脑的权限，比如说锁住了Ctrl键之类的[spoiler] 补药啊，没有ctrl键的话，瓦达西😭 [/spoiler] 就这样一场夺回电脑控制权的保卫战，就此拉开序幕... [h2] 打字玩法：简约却有细节 [/h2] 本作的玩法相当简单，就是根据眼球给予的词句，打出对应的拼音。 不过看似简单的玩法后也藏着不少贴心的设计： 首先是拼音是无需区分大小写的，输入后即可自动转换 其次打错字也不要紧，会有一个专属的提示音效，且无需删除错误内容，直接重新输入正确字母即可。 游戏会根据开局的打字清空自动设置难度，难度主要就影响打字倒计时的快慢（难度也可以自行调节） 当章节结束时后还会统计出错率和用时长短来给出一个综合评价[spoiler] 难道我真的在玩一个打字游戏？ [/spoiler] 不过游戏毕竟更偏向于剧情，这方面的难度也不会太高，如果是奔着纯打字体验而来的玩家可能会略感失望。 [h2] 核心体验：打破第四面墙，沉浸式恐惧与智斗[/h2] [b] 这部分内容含有部分剧透，请谨慎观看 [/b] 本作最亮眼的地方，便是不依赖猎奇画面与JumpScare 而是仅通过文字绑定现实的设定，营造出一种别样的沉浸感与恐惧感。 不同于传统恐怖游戏的视觉冲击，它的恶意藏在每一次按键中 你打出的每一句话，都会化作“现实”施加在你的电脑上 甚至在他的紧逼下你会被迫打出“献上左眼”“破坏CPU核心”“关闭防火墙”等致命指令， 而随之而来的屏幕闪烁、画面花屏、音效紊乱等场面，哪怕明知是游戏效果，也会忍不住担心电脑真的被破坏，而这也是正是其恐怖演出的精妙之处。 面对眼球的步步紧逼，所幸一只沉睡于设置界面的猫猫终于醒来，在它的帮助下你开始利用电脑的底层操作和游戏规则规避掉眼球的陷害 而到了游戏后期关卡时，随着一直帮助你的猫猫离去，你甚至要跳出游戏本身，打开本地文件夹，开开隐藏TXT文件从中寻找神秘网址与密码，才能推进剧情解锁猫猫复活，而眼球也得以解脱的真结局。 此外，游戏中设有直播模式，开启后修改真实steam昵称和避免真实IP泄露的风险，适合想要制作游戏视频或直播的玩家。 [h2] 隐藏成就指南 [/h2] 游戏一共有六个成就，其中四个成就是随着流程解锁，在这里给大家讲解一下如何完成剩下两个成就的解锁 1.你的签名 仍在 我这里哦。 [spoiler] 签下保证书后，打开设置按钮，选择“结束游戏”即可解锁 [/spoiler] 2.★★神奇打字大师★★ [spoiler] 这个成就有些复杂，需要在第六个关卡时，根据提示打开开发者模式 并根据TXT文件中的信息打出：C-SCR-MX 并点击按钮即可在关卡结束时触发 [/spoiler] [h2] 结语 [/h2] 作为一款的独立游戏，它的不足是显而易见的，那就是体量有限时长不足，但它的创意与诚意也的确值得肯定。 毕竟，在Meta游戏愈发稀缺的当下，能有这样一款游戏，让你在屏幕内外与一串代码、两颗颗眼球斗智斗勇，感受Mate的魅力，便已然足够珍贵。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 来一起感受游戏的乐趣喜欢这篇评论，也是可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

The game has a cute premise that starts off entertaining but wears thin as the hour goes by, especially as you realize that it is entirely deterministic. There is no agency for the player, Undertale this is not. You do not have any real control here despite what the floating eyes are telling you. You are not able to actually influence or control the narrative which means that the dialog starts to get tiring as it chides you for 'fighting' it over and over. Eventually the game will throw a puzzle at you so frustrating that you will either have to search for an external solution or just slam your keyboard randomly until you solve it. Ultimately, I refunded the game. Wait for a sale in my opinion.

有人说20多块就1.5h流程很亏，但是就我个人觉得这个游戏的创作和题材值得这个价格，这个游戏不仅仅是练习打字的助手，在幕后黑手慢慢诱导你“破坏电脑系统”的过程中我们也能看出当今信息社会的各种隐患存在，作者在教会我们各种电脑小技巧的同时也在叮嘱我们注意保护隐私安全的重要性，这无疑是一个好的出发点，最后真结局虽然包饺子了，但是也让我这种社畜感受到了心灵慰藉的温暖，我十分喜欢这个游戏。最后我想说一句：大眼睛可爱捏~

非常喜欢的一款小品游戏，在meta已经遍地走的当下玩出了别样的meta感。我从来没有想过在屏幕上打出文字这件事本身也具备meta定义的范畴，这样的强互动比拖拽鼠标的沉浸感更强，因为我对键盘的感知感受程度是远远大于鼠标的（按下去的声音、回馈的力道，屏幕上反馈的长条文字等）。与此同时，一般来说处理得很好的meta游戏会有三位主角，玩家、NPC、对玩家抱有强烈执念的NPC2。两位NPC的差分处理让我觉得很满意，如果流程能够更长更详尽一些就好了，非常感谢做出这样的作品

Dyping Escape takes an ordinary typing exercise and transforms it into an unsettling psychological horror experience that thrives on breaking expectations. Rather than focusing on monsters or combat, the game builds its identity around an eerie interaction with a mysterious floating pair of eyes that invites players into what initially appears to be an innocent typing challenge. From the very beginning, it becomes clear that every word entered on the keyboard carries significance, gradually pulling players into a disturbing digital mystery where the line between the game and reality begins to blur. The concept is refreshingly original, proving that horror can emerge from something as familiar as typing commands instead of relying on conventional survival mechanics. The gameplay revolves around accurately entering commands and phrases while responding to increasingly suspicious instructions. What starts as a simple test of typing speed steadily evolves into a psychological experiment where players are encouraged to question every action they perform. The game cleverly creates the illusion that typed commands are affecting the player's own computer, generating moments of tension that feel surprisingly convincing despite never placing the system at actual risk. This constant uncertainty becomes one of the game's strongest features, encouraging players to continue despite growing feelings of unease. The typing mechanic itself is engaging, rewarding both speed and precision while seamlessly integrating gameplay into the unfolding narrative. Storytelling is another area where Dyping Escape excels. The narrative slowly reveals the hidden secrets buried within an ancient game while introducing mysterious characters and unexpected allies. Among the most memorable elements is the appearance of a strange cat hidden deep within the game's code, offering guidance and hope against the sinister force controlling the experience. Instead of delivering its story through lengthy exposition, the game allows players to piece together events through dialogue, environmental clues, and the increasingly bizarre situations they encounter. This gradual approach keeps curiosity high from beginning to end and gives the relatively short adventure a satisfying emotional payoff. Atmosphere plays an equally important role in maintaining suspense. The retro-inspired visuals, minimalist presentation, and unsettling sound design combine to create an environment that constantly feels unpredictable. Rather than overwhelming players with graphic imagery or endless jump scares, the game relies on psychological discomfort, subtle audio cues, and the fear of making the wrong decision. The illusion that the game is interacting directly with the player's computer adds another layer of immersion, making even routine typing sequences feel stressful. This restrained approach demonstrates confidence in its concept and allows the horror to linger in the player's mind instead of depending on fleeting shock value. The expanded Steam version builds upon the foundation established by its original browser release, adding more narrative content, refined mechanics, and additional challenges. A scoring system encourages players to improve their typing performance by achieving higher ranks, giving the game replay value beyond its main storyline. Those who enjoy perfecting their accuracy or chasing top scores will find a reason to revisit the experience, while newcomers can appreciate how naturally the gameplay and storytelling complement one another throughout the adventure. The game does have a few shortcomings. Its relatively brief length means players seeking a lengthy horror campaign may finish it sooner than expected. Likewise, those looking for action-heavy gameplay or complex puzzles may find its emphasis on narrative and psychological tension somewhat limited. However, these are minor concerns when viewed against the game's originality, polished execution, and memorable presentation. Every aspect of the experience serves the central idea of turning typing into a source of suspense, and it succeeds remarkably well. Dyping Escape stands out as one of the more imaginative indie horror releases in recent years by combining interactive storytelling, typing-based gameplay, and fourth-wall-breaking psychological tricks into a cohesive package. It demonstrates that creative design and strong atmosphere can leave a lasting impression without requiring elaborate graphics or traditional horror formulas. Players interested in experimental horror, metafiction, or unique narrative experiences will likely find it to be an unforgettable journey that offers something genuinely different from the majority of games in the genre. Rating: 8/10

A mildly interesting "meta_horror" puzzle game about trying to defeat an evil typing game program. Meta, in the sense that the game that is openly a game in-universe, pony island style. Or Inscryption style. (Perhaps "we might as well call it "Daniel Mullens" style at this point...) My TL;DR is that it is an interesting game with annoyingly linear puzzle design and a lack of difficulty, that is ultimately saved by a more compelling back half and some genuinely good writing on the part of the game's primary antagonist and it's plight. Probably not worth $10, but if you get it on sale it's a cute little game. Massive Spoilers ahead, obviously. The game does a lot to act like it is going to hijack your computer specifically, but leaves an obvious barrier between your computer and the actual "in-game computer to make it clear that you're not actually in any real danger. It also extends the courtesy of allowing you disable the showing personal information. Helpful for streamers and anyone who wishes to opt out. There's an argument that such a barrier ruins immersion, but I'll take not being malware over true immersion any day. As for the game itself, it plays out rather simply. You go through multiple levels of this hypothetical typing game, which start as proper levels following public domain text, but quickly devolve into more abstract concepts like "the inside of your computer's hardware" and "your internet connection". You do this in order to try and obtain the contract that you sign at the beginning of the game, allowing you to be free of the game's control once and for all. The gameplay in these levels is where I think the game starts to stumble. You are put in a very simple track, where you are forced to type specific phrases. These phrases are taken as permission for the program to do whatever you tell it to, meaning that if you type something like "Please shoot me with a gun", then your character is getting shot. Effectively, you are battling with a fey-like creature who is trying to get you to give you permission to kill you. Thus, the solution to puzzles is finding ways to avoid this at all costs. Which is interesting. The main issue I have is that the game is extraordinarily linear with these solutions early on. You start with a cat ally who's entire purpose is to "enable" the use of certain options and methods of subverting the entity. Such as allowing you to open the menu which lets you change your gender, meaning that you can ensure you are no longer the gender of the entity you are typing out an elaborate punishment for. The issue with this is two-fold. One; the game's stakes and cat's dialogue (it explicitly says it only has limited ability to do what it does) can very easily lead you to believe that it is a limited time use hint system. The game is actually extremely generous with checkpoints. In fact, almost too much so, but I'll get to that later. In truth, the cat is not a hint system, the cat is straight up the solution for all of the early game puzzles. It will tell you what to do, and give you one thing to interact with. How exactly you must use this thing to subvert the creature is not particularly hard, so it is a case of needing to understand how little danger you are actually in. To some extent, I do understand this. It is much easier to plan around each level having it's own unique gimmick, so the cat acts as a way to "silo" specific solutions into their respective levels. This is especially important with the fact that these puzzles are timed, so you don't have much ability to mess around. The second issue comes crashing in when you realize that even within these levels, you must do things "in order" to progress. There's one level where the gimmick surrounds the fact that you can right-click and cut/delete/etc the text in order to avoid typing out anything horrid. The problem is that the means of doing this are fairly well known to anyone with a keyboard. You know that you can use a shortcut, or the right click menu, or the backspace button. These are each used as a solution, but in a specific order. The only way to know which one to use is to have the cat enable it for you in sequence, and then use it. If you are like me, and think of using the right click menu before the keyboard shortcut, then you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥. And even if you did think of the right one, you still have to click the damn cat. The game is much more of a haunted house roller coster ride with a unique theming, and realizing this destroys immersion. It's a case of the game suffering from what it does well, as it's visual presentation is in fact very good. The way effects of damage play out on the screen is very nice, and the extent to which they damage your ability to function makes it feel like you are slowly dying in a rather horrid way. Extremely fun. But that immersion is undercut by a refusal to let the player off their leash. If that were all, then I would hit a solid recommend and move on. But the back half of the game ultimately saves it. That damn cat gets pinned to a wall and it's powers primarily removed, leaving the player up to figure out the rest of the game. Most of the puzzles are still very linear, but require you to tab out of the window and start directly hunting through the files. The logic is obtuse enough that it requires some thought, and the cat now acts as an actual hint system, telling you what line to look at if you need a clue. You then also start to dig into the weeds surrounding the game's plot and the motivations of your foe, which could be gleaned prior, but come into greater focus now. Like the last act of Inscryption, you start to see your initial foe as more of a figure to be pitied rather than despised. The back and forth you have with the game's parser becomes a lot sharper, and the solutions are a lot more interesting and might actually have multiple ways to go about them, to a point. It feels like you are finally allowed to properly spar with this entity, and has a somewhat somber ending when you finally claim victory. A glimpse of what the game could have been, and I suspect the result of the developers starting to understand exactly what they were making. That combined with the presentation is enough to salvage the game for me, and makes it something I recommend, even if the $10 asking price might be slightly steep for the amount of quality content provided. I got this on sale for around $7, which I was happy with. So, I would call it a decent game. Sits in that realm being good enough to be enjoyable, while having enough glaring flaws to make the mind run wild with ideas and wonder how you would do it better. I look forward to seeing what the developers make next, and will be trying it out whenever it is made.
